summary: Kootenai NF crow's nest tree platform dated 1910, cabin added 1931, abandoned 1942; sources disagree on the first date and none describes the site today.

facts.design: Crow's nest tree platform; frame cabin added in 1931
facts.status_note: firelookout.com and the FFLA list both give abandoned, not gone or standing. No source we read describes what remains today.

events.note: firelookout.com says the present crow's nest tree platform was developed in 1910. The Lincoln County list gives an uncertain 192? for the site's start, a tree observation post; see resolved_conflicts.
A frame cabin was added at the site

corrections.why: The FFLA Montana list gives Lindy Peak the status Abandoned, not Gone. firelookout.com's page also says abandoned in 1942 and does not say the platform is gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com dates the present crow's nest tree platform to 1910. The Lincoln County list on montanalookouts.weebly.com dates the site's start, a tree observation post, to 192? (the 1920s, uncertain), which is later than 1910. The story reports both and says they disagree. The events list keeps 1910 because firelookout.com gives a full year for the present platform; the 192? date is uncertain and not settled.

The brief record lists firelookout.com as standing. The firelookout.com page says the site was abandoned in 1942 and describes no standing structure, and the FFLA list says Abandoned. Recorded as abandoned, not standing.

notes_for_editor: Two independent pages agree on abandonment; the first-structure date conflicts (1910 vs 192?). The firelookout.com standing-lookout map file (MTmapstanding.html) has a Lindy Peak marker. The map has no description and its text did not extract, so it is not used as evidence; it may explain the brief's standing flag. A Facebook post by a visitor (Byron Sanderson) appeared in search results and mentions remains and a site visit, but Facebook is login-walled in the cache, so it was not read or used. An editor who can read it could strengthen the today section. Record elevation 1,317.7 m matches 4,323 ft. Search budget: three WebSearch calls for this tower, one over the two-call limit.
